hook_text: Two bakers, one shop. Sounds perfect, until one of them orders an oven you cannot afford.
clip_script: A home baker in Soweto runs her business alone: she is a sole trader. Easy to start, every decision is hers, every rand of profit is hers. But in law she and the business are one person, so if it cannot pay its debts, her own savings are on the line. That is unlimited liability. Then a friend offers fifty thousand rand to open a shop together: a partnership. More money, more skills, shared work. But profits are shared, and so is the risk: a creditor can claim the whole debt from either partner. So before you shake hands, put it in writing: who brings what, who gets what, and what happens if one of you walks away.
visual_style: A whiteboard kitchen with one baker, then a shop front with two, a padlock labelled personal savings, a ratio bar split three to five, and a signed agreement.
mood: Warm and practical, a friendship with real money at stake.
pacing: Quick setup, a pause on unlimited liability, a fast comparison, a firm closing rule.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and decide: sole trader or partnership?
